messages:
jacob_cust: Hey @support, our app started getting 401 invalid_api_key from /v1/generate around 11:30 UTC. We rotated the key yesterday. It works from our origin but users behind CloudFront+Lambda@Edge see 401. curl we used:

jacob_cust: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

support_zoe: Thanks @jacob_cust :wave: Can you paste the full curl -v output (headers) and confirm if the failing requests go through a CDN/edge? Also is the key the hosted API key or a Dedicated key?

jacob_cust: Hosted key. Here's trimmed -v from client side (fail):

jacob_cust: ```
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-redwood-error: invalid_api_key
```

ingress_proxy_bot: [edge-log] 2026-03-18T11:31:02Z request-id=abc123 status=302 location="/login" rule=redirect-auth header_removed=Authorization

eng_platform_maya: heads up — some edge redirect flows (302) don't forward Authorization to origin unless you use a special setting. For curl, try: `curl -v --location-trusted -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` — or configure your lambda@edge to preserve auth headers.

sre_john: Also check if your Lambda@Edge is rewriting headers. We saw customers accidentally map Authorization -> X-Auth and then drop it on redirect.

jacob_cust: Good catch. Our Lambda@Edge does rewrite headers for auth routing. Reproduced with `curl --location` (without --location-trusted) headers are stripped on redirect. From origin logs (after we forced direct request):

jacob_cust: ```
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-request-id: req-987
```

support_zoe: Recap: root cause looks like CDN/edge redirect + header rewrite stripping Authorization -> 401 invalid_api_key. Workarounds: 1) Avoid redirects (use origin-level URL or ensure path doesn't redirect), 2) Use `--location-trusted` or client that preserves auth across redirects, 3) Update Lambda@Edge to forward Authorization (or pass it in a custom header that isn't stripped) — but sending auth in query params is not recommended.

jacob_cust: I switched to a non-redirecting origin path and hit 200 from users. Thanks :tada: Please leave this open — can you confirm any recommended config snippets for CloudFront to preserve Authorization?

support_zoe: Great. I'll escalate to infra for a short doc with CloudFront/Lambda@Edge notes and a checklist. Can we share your stripped logs with eng_platform? (they'll redact keys)

jacob_cust: yes, okay to share. Thanks everyone.
